extracted.intended_audience: BET readers interested in celebrity/lifestyle news and cultural controversy
extracted.subtask_description: News coverage of a makeup artist accused of doing blackface when transforming herself to look like Eddie Murphy; the piece frames evaluation around artistic intent, context (makeup tutorials/transformations), and public reaction. The article invites readers to judge whether the act is racist or excusable as artistic expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic expression defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the act qualify as artistic expression that excuses or explains the transformation? (Article: "Does she get a pass for artistic expression?")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the artist's stated defense: "Skin color didn't even enter my head." and her explanation that she "just wanted to paint myself as Eddie Murphy" and has similarly transformed into other famous figures (the Queen, Michael Jackson). The piece frames this as a question for readers to decide whether artistic intent mitigates accusations of racism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist's intent and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the creator's intent and the broader context of their work — e.g., whether the transformation is part of makeup tutorials/contouring demonstrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Jenna McDonnell "often shares photos... using makeup to transform into famous celebrities" and uses these posts to "show off her step-by-step guide contouring skills." Her apology and explanation ("I'm the least racist person") are presented as context for evaluating intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reaction and offensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how the audience perceives the act and whether it causes offense, including direct accusations of racism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece highlights commenter reactions (example: "Dumb white b****," and multiple comments claiming she's "racist"). It reports the artist felt "sick" at the response and apologized: "I'm so so sorry if it offends anyone." Public backlash is presented as a key factor in judging the act's acceptability.
